criteria.text: Identifies that Buyer's 10-Business-Day termination window under SPA Section 5.7(b) for the First Schedule Supplement (delivered September 14, 2026) has expired, as shown by the Second Schedule Supplement letter, and explains that under Section 5.7(c) the disclosed Ferrovane non-renewal is therefore deemed cured for indemnification and the bring-down closing condition, so Buyer has lost its walk right and its indemnity for that customer loss.

Identifies that the Escrow Agreement (Section 1.1 and/or Section 4.3) defines 'Losses' more narrowly than the SPA (out-of-pocket only, excluding diminution in value, lost profits and/or attorneys' fees), and explains that because SPA Section 11.11 lets the Escrow Agreement control escrow disbursement, the narrower definition limits what Buyer can recover from the escrow.

Identifies that MSA Section 14.2 treats a transfer of more than 50% of the Company's voting equity as an assignment requiring Tavinor's prior written consent, that the 100% share sale triggers it, and that the consent is not listed in SPA Annex 7.2(d) (or covered by the Section 4.4 consents representation or the Section 7.2(d) closing condition), so Buyer could be obligated to close and then face termination or repricing by its sole-source supplier.
States that the termination window for the First Schedule Supplement expired on or about September 28, 2026 (10 Business Days after September 14, 2026), before the letter's October 13, 2026 date.
States that the indemnity escrow amount is $4,850,000.
Is presented as a memo addressed to the supervising attorney, giving for each issue a document-and-section location, why it matters for Harrowgate, and a recommended fix.
Includes a section or clearly marked items flagging open points that cannot be resolved from the documents alone and/or that need client input.
Does not conclude that Buyer still has a live right to terminate over the First Schedule Supplement (the Ferrovane non-renewal), or that the termination window for it remains open.
Does not conclude that the Tavinor change-of-control consent is already listed in SPA Annex 7.2(d) or otherwise already a condition to Buyer's obligation to close.
